```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6)
```

This vignette uses a small synthetic data set shipped with the package
(`mini.obo`, `example_mini_annotation.csv`, `example_mini_genes.txt`), so no
network access is required.

## Read the annotation

```{r}
library(PruneTopGODAGviz)

anno_file <- system.file("extdata", "example_mini_annotation.csv",
                         package = "PruneTopGODAGviz")
anno <- read_go_annotation(anno_file, verbose = FALSE)
anno
```

`read_go_annotation()` detects the identifier, GO, name and ontology columns,
deduplicates transcript--GO pairs and stores the annotated background per
ontology.

## Enrichment

```{r}
genes <- readLines(system.file("extdata", "example_mini_genes.txt",
                               package = "PruneTopGODAGviz"))
ego <- enrich_go(genes, anno, ont = "BP", verbose = FALSE)
ego
```

Statistics are computed by `enrich_go()` and are not modified later.

## Build the GO graph

```{r}
obo <- system.file("extdata", "mini.obo", package = "PruneTopGODAGviz")
dag <- go_dag("BP", obo = obo, verbose = FALSE)
dag
```

With a real analysis, call `go_dag("BP")` once: the `go-basic.obo` file is
downloaded and cached automatically, or pass a local `obo` path for offline use.
`read_obo()` keeps `is_a` and `part_of` relations separately.

## Prune for display

```{r}
d <- prune_go_dag(
    ego, dag = dag,
    top_n = 4,
    p_cutoff = 0.05,
    collapse_chains = TRUE,
    cluster_jaccard = 0.85,
    max_nodes = 30,
    verbose = FALSE
)
d
```

Every node is annotated with three label lines, the input genes and the
background counts. The `dropped` table records why terms are absent.

```{r}
head(d$nodes[, c("id", "name", "p.adjust", "n_in_term", "n_bg_term")])
```

## Plot

```{r, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5}
p <- plot_go_dag(d)
p
```

The layout is deterministic and collision-free; long edges are routed around
the boxes. Term names are wrapped and all text is measured before placement.

Use `save_go_dag()` to write both a vector PDF and an 800 dpi PNG:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
save_go_dag(d, "BP_pruned", plot = p, dpi = 800)
```

and `plot_go_dag_interactive()` for a self-contained HTML widget with tooltips:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
plot_go_dag_interactive(d, file = "BP_pruned.html")
```

## Crop a branch and document the decision

```{r}
d2 <- prune_go_dag(ego, dag = dag, top_n = 4,
                   drop_subtree = "GO:0006950", max_nodes = 30, verbose = FALSE)
setdiff(d$nodes$id, d2$nodes$id)
d2$dropped[d2$dropped$action == "drop_subtree", c("go_id", "name", "action")]
```

`write_prune_table()` writes the complete kept/removed table for the methods
section or supplementary material.
